To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
co-location information has a significant negative effect on location privacy, and that this problem cannot be addressed by existing location-privacy protection solutions.
the privacy risks of a user are significantly higher when co-location information about her is considered by an adversary.

(a) the co-location information can significantly degrade the users’ location privacy, even in the absence of other sources of information; (b) the privacy loss is more severe when the adversary has access to more co-location information; and (c) the users’ location-privacy protection mechanism can be designed to minimize the privacy loss due to co-location information.

a novel privacy threat that is caused by the increasing availability of co-location information about users.
the problem of quantifying interdependent privacy risks with co-locations, a problem that is of high importance for the users of online social networking services.

the privacy implications of the increasingly common practice of co-locating with other users in social networks and other online systems, and provides the first comprehensive study on how to quantify the resulting privacy risks.
